summary.text: André Carson is the Democratic incumbent for Indiana's 7th Congressional District (Indianapolis). An Indianapolis native who worked in law enforcement and state counterterrorism work and served briefly on the City-County Council, he won a March 2008 special election to succeed his late grandmother, Rep. Julia Carson. He is a member of the House Intelligence Committee and a Senior Whip for House Democrats.

paragraphs.text: Born in Indianapolis in 1974 and raised on the city's east side; graduated from Arsenal Technical High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice management from Concordia University-Wisconsin and a master's in business management from Indiana Wesleyan University.

Worked in law enforcement before office, including as a compliance officer with the Indiana State Excise Police (1996-2005), and later in the anti-terrorism division of the Indiana Department of Homeland Security, including at the Indiana Intelligence Fusion Center.
Was a Democratic precinct committeeperson in Indianapolis and, in 2007, was chosen at a Marion County Democratic caucus to fill a seat on the Indianapolis City-County Council, serving until 2008.
Won a March 11, 2008 special election to the 7th District seat after the death of his grandmother, Rep. Julia Carson, who had held it since 1997; he was sworn in March 13, 2008.
Was the second Muslim ever elected to the U.S. Congress.

Serves on the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence (National Intelligence Enterprise; National Security Agency and Cyber), the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Railroads, Pipelines and Hazardous Materials), and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party for the 2025-2026 Congress.

According to his House biography, he chaired the Intelligence Committee's Counterterrorism, Counterintelligence, and Counterproliferation Subcommittee, which held the first congressional hearing on Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in more than 50 years, and he serves as a Senior Whip for the House Democratic Caucus. He is a former member of the House Financial Services Committee.
Belongs to caucuses including the Congressional Black Caucus, the Progressive Caucus, the New Democrat Coalition, and the LGBT Equality Caucus, according to his House biography.
